subject: geography
title: Place Attachment & Identity
welcome_lead: Examine how place identity is constructed.
meta_desc: A-Level Geography AQA adventure on place attachment, identity and lived experience.
final_note: Places blend physical fabric with human meaning.

concepts.def: Location imbued with meaning through experience and culture.
Emotional bond linking people to specific places.
Embedded local knowledge; rituals, slang, hidden spaces.
External view; first impressions, official descriptions.
Internal: location, geology, demography, land use.
External: trade, migration, government policy, climate.

walkthroughs.body_html: Hidalgo and Hernandez (2001) identify physical attachment (built environment) and social attachment (community ties). Length of residence, life events (birth, marriage), shared narratives all build attachment. Long-term residents of mining valleys (Rhondda) retain attachment despite economic decline.

Endogenous: Liverpool's port location, sandstone geology, Cathedral. Exogenous: Atlantic trade, Irish migration (Famine 1840s), TNC investment. Most places' character results from interaction of both. Globalisation increases exogenous influences relative to endogenous.

Stratford (London) transformed by 2012 Olympics. Endogenous: marshy Lea Valley, industrial decline. Exogenous: £9 billion Olympic investment, Crossrail. New postcode E20 created. Insider Bangladeshi community vs outsider Olympic visitor experiences differ sharply. Westfield mall 320 shops.
